And when he heard that Muzaffar al-Din had left and gone to Erbil,
he went to Tell Afar and took it by battle.
Then al-Malik al-Ashraf son of al-Adil,
who was at that time in Harran,
came to Resh'ayna (Ra's al-'Ayn).
And he made an agreement with Muzaffar al-Din, the lord of Erbil,
and with the lord of Amid and of Hisn Kifa,
and with the lord of Jazira,
and with the lord of Dara,
that they should not permit Nur al-Din to take anything from the territory of the lord of Sinjar.
And they all came to Nisibis,
and from there they came to Beth 'Arbaye.
And Nur al-Din went to Kafar Zammar,
and from there to Bawashzaha.
And when they camped to rest,
because they were exhausted,
the armies of al-Ashraf and those who were with him mounted and encountered Nur al-Din,
and the party of Nur al-Din was broken with a terrible defeat.
And Nur al-Din fled, and with four persons escaped to Mosul.
And the men of the house of al-Ashraf entered the territory of Mosul,
and took captives and burned;
especially in the city of Balad they caused great destruction.
It is told
that a woman was cooking a meal,
and when she heard of the pillagers, she took two bracelets off her wrist,
and hid them in the fire, and fled.
Then one of the horsemen entered into that same house,
seeking something to eat.
And he found nothing in that house except a single egg;
and he took it and came to the fire to roast it.
And as he was raking the fire,
he found the bracelets in it.
And this was a wondrous chance.
And they remained for many days devastating the country,
with envoys going and coming between them.
And Nur al-Din restored Tell Afar to his cousin,
and peace was made;
and afterward the armies dispersed.
And in that same year, when the Franks had taken Constantinople,
they grew very bold,
and went out to the land of Phoenicia,
and took captives as far as the Jordan,
and wrought a great slaughter among the Arabs.
And they came against Hama,
and its lord, Nasir al-Din son of Taqi al-Din son of Shahanshah son of Ayyub, went out and met them,
and he was badly defeated,
and he fled and entered Hama.
And the Arab citizens of the town went out to fight with the Franks,
and they were all killed.
Then al-Malik al-Adil sent to them,
and gave them Nazareth and all the districts whose revenues used to be divided by half between the Franks and the Arabs;
